Incorporating SLOOS into the assessment:

- Credit supply: SLOOS indicates broad easing of lending standards across residential real estate (including jumbo/QM and HELOCs), CRE (multifamily and nonfarm nonresidential), and consumer credit (credit cards, auto). Banks also increased credit limits on cards and reduced auto loan rates; few originated subprime. This points to accommodative bank lending conditions that support growth and employment.
- Credit demand: Reported demand was stronger for consumer loans and CRE at foreign banks, mixed-to-weaker for C&I and auto in the current quarter, but banks expect stronger demand ahead for C&I and credit cards. This suggests improving momentum into the near term despite some sectoral softness.
- Interaction with FSR risks: Easier mortgage/CRE credit can reinforce elevated housing valuations and CRE sensitivities flagged in the FSR, but strong bank capital/liquidity and accommodative funding conditions remain supportive.
- Policy read-through: Against elevated inflation and a faster taper, easier bank credit availability reduces downside risks to activity and labor markets, partially offsetting the FSR’s caution.

Net effect: Relative to the FSR-tilted baseline, SLOOS makes the outlook modestly more constructive on growth/credit transmission, though not enough to outweigh inflation and stability concerns. Adjusting upward modestly.
